In order to improve the adhesion and road grip, and to prevent the risk of sliding and skidding, the following action is recommended:
Start off / move away, with the wheels straight (aligned) in the highest gear possible, normally second gear. Raise the clutch slowly and smoothly and accelerate smoothly and gently.
Travel at a speed that is suited to the weather conditions and (this means engaging the highest gear possible) compatible with safety. questions.question:
Las personas mayores pueden sufrir más accidentes de circulación en situaciones...
Elderly people may have more traffic accidents in situations...
questions.help:
Road traffic collisions              
               
6. Groups of drivers most at risk of a collision    
6.2 The elderly
Older people who have suffered a deterioration of psychomotor skills that are important for driving (such as a reduced ability to concentrate or an increase in the time it takes to react) may have more collisions in complex situations that require quick response, especially at junctions and at the entries and exits of roads when driving at high speed.
Conversely, in situations when there is enough time to react, they have the same problems as other younger people. Due to this, you must give the elderly enough time and not put pressure on them.
(Página 255 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.question:
Los síntomas de las alergias respiratorias pueden producir...
Symptoms of respiratory allergies may lead to…
questions.help:
ILLNESS AND MEDICATION
 
20 Some illnesses that can affect driving
20.1 Respiratory allergies
Allergic rhinitis can reduce the psycho-physical fitness to drive by up to 42%, causing alterations such as the loss of efficiency, lack of attention, a lower concentration level and decreased ability of visual coordination. It reduces the ability to judge stopping distance, thus increasing the risk of a collision.
The most common symptoms of this illness are very similar to those of a simple cold: Runny nose, watery eyes, blurred vision, bouts of sneezing (sometimes up to 20 in a row), fatigue, headache, and so on.
(Página 46 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.question:
El sistema de aviso de colisión frontal con detección de peatones y ciclistas (FCW+P+C), ¿cómo avisa a la persona conductora ante una colisión inminente?
How does the forward collision warning system with pedestrian and cyclist (FCW+P+C) detection warn the driver of an imminent collision?
questions.help:
Road traffic collisions                
                 
RISK GROUPS              
5 Pedestrians        
5.3.1 Forward Collision Warning with detection of Pedestrians and Cyclists (FCW+P+C)
This system monitors conditions on the road and in the surrounding area, warning the driver when it estimates a high probability of collision with other vehicles or with pedestrians or cyclists. It uses an acoustic or visual signal or vibration to alert the driver.
Under no circumstances does the system act on the steering of the vehicle; it is only a warning system and the driver is solely responsible for taking the action necessary to prevent a collision or avoid hitting a pedestrian.
(Página 253 del manual 'Learning to drive')
